transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2027-08-04 14:30 PDT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees (Redwood): Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair, Carlos Mendez
- Attendees (Alderbrook Health): Michael Torres, Dr. Sara Levin, Anika Rao, Jonah Park, Talia Chen

Auto-summary (auto-generated; may be rough):
Redwood and Alderbrook ran through procurement gate checklist for MSA/DPA, clarified data residency/egress, KMS and SSO needs, and scoped a short technical pilot. Customer asked for SLA language clarifications around latency and incident response, and a pricing credit for initial pilot. Action items were assigned: Redwood to return redlines and SE to deliver benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Commercial route (MSA/DPA redlines, billing path)
- Security (SOC2, KMS, data residency, SSO/SAML)
- SLA specifics (availability, incident response, latency targets)
- Pilot scope and acceptance criteria
- Pricing and short-term credits for pilot

[00:00] Liam O'Connor: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. We're gonna run through the procurement gate items, make sure we hit MSA/DPA redlines, security, and the pilot scope. Priya will cover the technical baseline. Michael?
[00:18] Michael Torres: Yep thanks Liam, and thanks to everyone. We're basically at vendor approval committee next week so need to make sure legal and infosec have what they need, and finance wants a clear pilot cost and SLA for approval.
[00:34] Priya Nair: Hi all, quick intro from me, I'm covering SE side - I'll own the perf spreadsheet and the test plan we discussed. I'll also do a short write-up on VPC/private deployment options, and show where Dedicated vs Hosted sit in the risk model.
[00:51] Dr. Sara Levin: Thanks. For us the big blockers are encryption at rest with customer managed keys, audit logs, and egress controls. We host PHI-ish metadata so need clarity on data flows and residency.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. On Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS (HSM integrations), audit logs, and you can run a Private VPC control plane. We'll note the exact KMS providers supported, but generally we do KMS through AWS KMS or bring-your-own HSM — we need to check HSM vendor list for your procurement.
[01:38] Jonah Park: Quick legal note — are you offering any tiered SLAs for incident response and availability? Our procurement team typically wants a 99.9% uptime with credits spelled out. Also, retention terms in DPA are important.
[01:56] Carlos Mendez: We can definitely map SLA tiers. For Hosted customers we publish a standard SLA; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can negotiate enterprise SLAs. For pilot we usually propose a trial SLA and carve out credit structure for production-level SLAs once capacity is reserved.
[02:15] Talia Chen: Finance will want to see how billing works if we exceed pilot usage — is there an overage rate or auto-billing? We also want to avoid unexpected egress fees.
[02:32] Priya Nair: We'll include an expected cost model with typical token/unit assumptions, and show how autoscale/burst capacity would affect billing. Egress fees are cloud-provider side but we can model network egress and we can also provide a private peering option to reduce network transit.
[02:55] Michael Torres: Ok good. On the MSA/DPA redlines, Jonah and I flagged two templates: one on liability cap and one on data deletion timeline. We'd like deletion within 30 days for derivatives and 7 days for raw logs — is that compatible?
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: The standard DPA has 30 days for customer data deletion; logs are often at 90 by default, but we can negotiate shorter retention for pilot. For certain hosted products, there may be system logs needed for debugging, but we can pseudonymize and limit retention. We'll put proposed language in the redline doc.
[03:43] Dr. Sara Levin: Also need confirmation on inbound model telemetry — we do not want model outputs sent to third-party telemetry by default.
[03:53] Priya Nair: Understood. Our telemetry for hosted is opt-in; for Private we keep telemetry local. Will confirm exact flags in the platform that turn on telemetry or anonymize it.
[04:12] Michael Torres: A few procurement process questions: what approvals do we need from your side, and what's the typical lead time for Dedicated capacity?
[04:28] Carlos Mendez: For Dedicated it's a capacity planning process — typically 4–8 weeks depending on GPU availability and region. If you need faster, we can do an initial hosted pilot with guaranteed throughput then transition to Dedicated once procurement clears.
[04:45] Jonah Park: Re: region — we require data to stay in US-east for this pilot. Is that supported?
[04:56] Priya Nair: Yes, we have US-east and US-west control planes for Private and Hosted. For strict region controls we recommend Private in your VPC; that will ensure traffic and storage stay in US-east.
[05:12] Talia Chen: Are there any export control / ITAR concerns we should flag? We do have some regulated datasets.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: We can coordinate with legal on export controls; Redwood has an export-control checklist we can share. For ITAR-level data we'd probably suggest on-prem or air-gapped deployments. We'll surface that in the redlines.
[05:39] Michael Torres: Great. On pricing: can we get a pilot credit or reduced rate while we evaluate? The procurement committee expects some offset to cover testing.
[05:53] Liam O'Connor: We typically offer a pilot credit structure — often a usage credit or a fixed cost discount — we can show a few pricing pathways: pure usage-hosted, committed Dedicated, or a hybrid. I'll send a commercial summary with a recommended pilot credit we discussed internally.
[06:12] Dr. Sara Levin: For security attachments, we need SOC 2 Type II report and penetration test summary. Is that available?
[06:21] Carlos Mendez: Yes, we can provide our SOC 2 artifacts and a pen test summary under an NDA. We'll attach those to the security packet.
[06:34] Priya Nair: Jumping to the SLA language you asked about: are you more concerned about availability metrics or latency tail behavior? They are related but different — some of our customers push for P99 latency SLAs for certain interactive endpoints.
[06:52] Dr. Sara Levin: P99 latency is important; clinician workflows are sensitive to long tails. We need guarantees or at least an operational plan for tails beyond 500ms on average interactive calls.
[07:10] Priya Nair: For interactive chat flows we can propose a P99 SLA target of X ms — I'll pull numbers from our telemetry and provide realistic P50/P95/P99 guidance in the perf baseline. Note that P99 varies by sequence length and model choice; we'll show model-specific profiles.
[07:33] Michael Torres: When you say model choice, are you recommending specific open models for cost vs latency trade-offs?
[07:41] Priya Nair: Yep — we can supply model recommendations. For example a smaller distilled model for short Q&A, a larger one for summarization. Also quantized variants on Dedicated give large cost savings. We'll put a mapping in the doc.
[07:59] Jonah Park: Legal question on indemnity — standard clause says Redwood indemnifies for IP claims with standard thresholds. We may ask to tighten on third-party claims tied to model outputs.
[08:15] Liam O'Connor: We can discuss carve-outs topic-by-topic; we've seen similar requests and usually negotiate IP indemnities with thresholds tied to usage and breach scenarios. I'll flag for legal.
[08:30] Talia Chen: Any technical acceptance criteria for the pilot? Platform uptime, latency, and data handling?
[08:39] Priya Nair: Proposed acceptance criteria: 1) endpoints meet P95 latency target for defined prompt sets; 2) model output quality pass rate on a small eval set (we'll propose metrics); 3) no data exfiltration incidents and successful KMS key rotations. We'll detail pass/fail thresholds.
[08:59] Michael Torres: Ok, perfect. On the DPA: can we get a clause for breach notification within 24 hours?
[09:07] Jonah Park: Yes, 24 hours is our expectation.
[09:12] Liam O'Connor: We'll push for strong but mutually reasonable times; 24 hours for acknowledged incidents is doable. We'll propose wording.
[09:22] Dr. Sara Levin: Also want to confirm logging retention window and who can access logs. We need role-based access controls and ability to export audit logs to our SIEM.
[09:35] Carlos Mendez: Role-based access exists in the platform; we can set SSO/SAML and RBAC groups. Audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM or delivered via secure bucket. We'll include the integration steps.
[09:51] Priya Nair: Quick note on private deployments: if you choose Private in your VPC, audit logs are fully under your control and we can set up direct delivery to your SIEM. For Hosted we can stream via secure connectors under contract.
[10:10] Michael Torres: Any blockers around KMS? We want BYOK — bring your own keys.
[10:17] Priya Nair: BYOK supported. We'll enumerate supported KMS providers and HSM options in the security packet. Key rotation processes and backup procedures will be documented.
[10:27] Talia Chen: For pricing approvals, do you require a PO up front for Dedicated?
[10:33] Carlos Mendez: For Dedicated we typically require a commitment (monthly/annual) and a PO or contract signature. For the pilot we can do a smaller commitment or hosted usage.
[10:43] Michael Torres: Let's talk about timeline. Procurement committee meets 2027-08-12. We need MSA/DPA redlines to review on 2027-08-09 ideally.
[10:53] Liam O'Connor: We'll commit to sending redlines by 2027-08-09. Priya will send the perf baseline by 2027-08-10. Carlos will attach SOC2 and pen test artifacts under NDA by 2027-08-09.
[11:08] Jonah Park: Great. A few micro-questions from legal — do you support audit rights, and what's the process for on-site audits?
[11:18] Liam O'Connor: We have audit rights language in the enterprise addendum; for on-site audits we can discuss limited-scope audits and a redacted environment. We'll add detail on the audit process.
[11:31] Dr. Sara Levin: One more, regarding model updates: how are model changes communicated and can we lock a model for production?
[11:40] Priya Nair: You can pin model versions for production. We also have release notes and a model deprecation window; we'll include a rollback and canary policy in the rollout section.
[11:54] Michael Torres: Ok sounds like a plan. Can you also include a brief comparison to a couple competitors in the commercial packet? Procurement sometimes asks why choose Redwood vs other providers.
[12:05] Liam O'Connor: Sure — we'll include a brief competitive positioning page focusing on latency cost economics and private deployment options.
[12:17] Talia Chen: One last callout — we need clarity on data residency for backups and DR. Where are backups stored?
[12:26] Priya Nair: Backups follow your region and storage settings; for Private we keep them in your VPC/region, and for Hosted we use region-scoped storage. We'll document retention and DR practices.
[12:40] Carlos Mendez: Ok, to recap next steps — we'll send MSA/DPA redlines, security packet (SOC2/pen test), perf baseline and pilot plan, and a commercial summary with suggested pilot credit. Customer to confirm procurement timeline and run internal approvals.
[12:59] Michael Torres: Thanks — if procurement wants minor redlines that's fine but please keep us in the loop. We'll aim to have a decision after the 8/12 committee.
[13:10] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all. Anything else before we wrap?
[13:15] Dr. Sara Levin: No that's it. We'll review materials and circle back.
[13:20] Liam O'Connor: Great, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels were approximate; there may be minor transcription errors (e.g., 'K-V cache' for KV cache, 'Red Wood Private' spelled differently). There was occasional crosstalk when legal and security spoke over each other.

END TRANSCRIPT
